transitions.scope: Requires free active-site lysine, not the enamine-bound lysine after step3. Enzyme-dependent fluorescence loss is observed and interpreted by the authors using their product-iminium model; neither covalent occupancy nor individual formation/dissociation rates are measured here. Product-only incubation has its own source conditions in the contextual evidence.

fit_models.regime: Soluble subsaturating substrate, initial fluorescence slope before the first turnover, little accumulated product and enzyme concentrations below the product-rebinding Kd in the source assay.
fit_models.scope: A composite second-order coefficient through the reporter-product boundary (source steps1-3). The source describes the limiting transition state within this path, not an observed time-resolved trajectory or any individual arrow rate. It does not identify separate kcat, substrate KM, steps4-5, full-cycle turnover, or product-sequestration rates.

source_model.source_abstraction: Figure1 names major steps and explicitly omits proton transfers, binding events and some intermediates. Its reversible arrows are source-model directions, not experimental measurements of each microscopic process.

deposit_absence_reason: No retained RA61 ligand/coordinate arrangement is bound. Main Figure2 is a design model; its caption says the experimental structure lacked ligand and the substrate orientation is unknown.

reporter_context.observed: Enzyme-dependent fluorescence loss upon incubation with added product; RA61 shows minor progress-curve curvature at low enzyme concentration and greater curvature at higher concentration. RA34 has the pronounced burst-like example.
reporter_context.author_model: Product sequestration reduces free enzyme available for catalysis and reduces the fluorescence assigned to free aldehyde. Signal loss is not a measurement of total product loss or reaction yield; the authors attribute it to reversible product association/iminium formation.
reporter_context.initial_window_assumption: The early calibrated fluorescence signal reports aldehyde formation with negligible product-rebinding interference under the source low-product conditions; this is not an orthogonal verification or a mathematical guarantee.
reporter_context.product_binding_scope: The source conditional apparent Kd is an approximate upper limit under an assumed bound-product fluorescence, not a microscopic iminium equilibrium/rate, substrate KM, or on-path intermediate affinity. Preserve the original 26/17/10 uM alternatives and their assumptions together; do not turn them into an uncertainty interval or a new common scalar fit.
reporter_context.burst_inference: Product-related curvature does not supply rates for source steps4-5. The free-enzyme pool can bind product before a whole turnover when enzyme is in excess; steps4-5 in the source path regenerate that pool, but are not a universal temporal prerequisite for rebinding.

residue_scope.scope: Lys176 belongs to the Figure2 design model. The retained fluorescence and pH evidence do not directly map the product attachment to that residue; no sequence, MS or coordinate match is inferred.

limitations: The observed optical behavior and source-proposed covalent chemistry have distinct evidence status.
The substrate-derived on-path iminium and aldehyde-derived off-path Schiff-base species are different; neither label establishes complete protonation or reacted atom identity.
Chemical participants, proton balance, exact conformers and microscopic rates are not validated by this symbolic source-model relation.
No exact protein sequence or physical assay-preparation identity, new experiment, independently reviewed mechanism, registry admission or enzyme-design performance is established.

acquisition.scope: Retained main/SI reused offline. Acquisition receipt and Jiang2008 appendix retain cumulative consumption; no source bodies redistributed.

reconsideration.bespoke_code: Generic initial second-order fit role and measurement boundary, explicit input-reaction lineage distinct from bound ligand identity, and a resolver for contextual evidence objects; no enzyme-ID branch or atom-specific adapter.
reconsideration.reuse: Existing observations, assay, source witnesses and complete reporter-boundary object reused. This is a third enzyme context and second publication for the source-model consumer; no measured curation-time saving.
reconsideration.incremental_value: Previously retained prose becomes source-bound path/endpoint topology distinguishing substrate iminium from product sequestration. No new biological conclusion or superiority to competent source reading is claimed.

reaction_branch_scope: The reaction_branch_id indexes the source substrate reaction lineage, including its products. It does not assert unchanged chemical identity, bound occupancy or validated molecular participant balance in each source-drawn species set.
